body_text: Parents Warned After Popular Kids’ Bottle Is Recalled Due to Loose Part Hazard A popular children’s product sold across the UK has been urgently recalled after safety checks revealed a potential choking hazard. Parents and guardians have been advised to stop children from using the item immediately and to keep it away from young children until it has been returned or safely disposed of. The recalled product is a Toy Story themed water bottle sold by discount retailer Home Bargains. The recall was issued after it was discovered that the bottle’s spout may detach from the lid during use. This creates a small loose component that could become a choking risk for children. The product was available for purchase from May 2026 as part of a promotional release linked to the launch of Pixar’s Toy Story 5 movie. Customers who purchased the affected bottles are being asked to check the batch information and return any impacted items for a full refund. Which Toy Story Water Bottles Are Affected? The recall applies only to specific batches of the Toy Story water bottle sold through Home Bargains stores. The affected batch numbers are: 11449732 11449736 11449737 11449738 11449742 11449743 11449744 Customers should check the batch code on the product price tag or the care label inside the bottle to confirm whether their item is included in the recall. At this time, no other batches of the Toy Story water bottle have been reported as affected. Why Has the Children’s Bottle Been Recalled? The main concern identified with the product is the possibility that the spout can separate from the lid. If this happens, the detached piece may become small enough for a child to place in their mouth, increasing the risk of choking. Young children are particularly vulnerable to choking incidents because they may not recognise unsafe objects or understand the danger of loose parts. Products designed for children are therefore subject to strict safety standards to reduce risks caused by detachable components. The recall highlights the importance of regularly checking children’s products for damage, loose parts, or signs of wear, even when the item appears to be working normally. What Should Parents Do If They Own the Recalled Bottle? TJ Morris, the company behind Home Bargains, has advised customers to stop using the recalled water bottle immediately. Parents and carers should: Stop allowing children to use the bottle. Keep the product away from children. Check the batch number to confirm whether it is affected. Return the bottle to the nearest Home Bargains store. Request a full refund. Customers do not need to have the original packaging to return the item. If they are unsure whether their bottle is included in the recall, they can still take it to a store for assistance. Home Bargains has apologised to customers for any inconvenience caused by the recall. How Product Recalls Help Protect Children Child safety recalls are an important way of preventing injuries caused by products that may not meet expected safety standards. Companies issue recalls when they discover a possible danger, allowing customers to remove potentially unsafe items from homes. Parents should stay informed about product recalls, especially for items commonly used by children such as: Water bottles and cups Toys Baby equipment Clothing with small attachments School accessories Checking official recall notices can help families identify risks early and take action before an accident occurs. Tips for Keeping Children Safe Around Everyday Products While manufacturers work to ensure products are safe, parents can take additional steps to reduce risks at home. Some useful safety habits include: Inspect Children’s Items Regularly Look for cracks, broken pieces, loose parts, or damage that could create a hazard. Items used daily can become worn over time. Follow Age Recommendations Always use products according to the manufacturer’s age guidance. Items designed for older children may contain parts that are unsuitable for younger children. Remove Damaged Products If a toy, bottle, or accessory becomes damaged, it is safer to stop using it rather than attempt a temporary repair. Stay Updated With Recall Announcements Government websites, retailer notices, and official company announcements regularly publish information about unsafe products. Retailer Response and Customer Advice TJ Morris has confirmed that affected Toy Story water bottles should be returned to Home Bargains stores for a full refund. The company has encouraged customers to follow the recall instructions and avoid using any affected products. The recall only applies to the listed batch numbers. Customers who own a similar bottle from another batch should check official updates if they have concerns. Conclusion The recall of the Toy Story children’s water bottle serves as an important reminder for families to check everyday products carefully. Although the item was popular among children, the potential for the spout to detach created a serious choking concern. Parents who purchased the affected bottles should stop using them immediately and return them to Home Bargains for a refund. Staying aware of product recalls and safety warnings can help protect children from avoidable risks. Sources Home Bargains product recall notice issued by TJ Morris regarding the Toy Story water bottle recall. The Sun, published 4 August 2026. UK product safety guidance and recall information provided through official consumer safety channels. Disclaimer This article is written for general information purposes only and is based on publicly available recall information at the time of writing. Consumers should check official retailer announcements and government safety notices for the latest updates. If you believe you own a recalled product, follow the manufacturer’s or retailer’s instructions before allowing children to use it.

title: Employee Background Verification Checklist for Indian Startups & SMBs [2026]
summary: The complete background verification checklist for Indian startups and SMBs. Step-by-step process, required documents, compliance requirements, and recommended tools.
body_text: Insights & Resources Employee Background Verification Checklist for Indian Startups & SMBs [2026] August 19, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet Most Indian startups skip background verification entirely until something goes wrong — a fake degree surfaces three months into employment, a hire’s identity documents don’t match payroll records, or a reference check that was never conducted would have revealed a pattern of misconduct. By then, the cost of a bad hire has already compounded through wasted training, damaged client relationships, and the expense of rehiring. This checklist gives Indian startups and SMBs a practical, step-by-step framework for building a background verification process that catches problems before they start — without the overhead and complexity designed for enterprises with 10,000 employees. The 7-Point Background Verification Checklist 1. Identity Document Verification What to verify: Confirm the candidate’s legal identity by validating government-issued documents against official databases. Documents to check: PAN Card — Validates tax identity and legal name. Required for salary processing, TDS deductions, and EPF enrollment. This is the single most critical identity check for any Indian employer. Voter ID — Provides a second government-issued identity proof with photograph, name, and address. Useful for cross-referencing against PAN data. Driving Licence — Contains name, date of birth, address, and photograph. Essential for roles involving driving responsibilities, but valuable as a secondary identity document for any hire. UAN (Universal Account Number) — Links to the candidate’s EPF history. Verifying UAN confirms employment history claims and provident fund contribution records. How to do it efficiently: Use a platform like Compose1 Verify that bundles PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, and UAN checks into a single workflow. The platform’s cross-record comparison automatically flags discrepancies across documents — different names, mismatched dates of birth, or inconsistent identity signals — which is far more reliable than checking each document in isolation. Red flags to watch for: Name spelled differently across documents (minor variations in transliteration are common and may not be fraudulent, but significant differences warrant investigation) Date of birth mismatch between PAN and other documents PAN number that returns “inactive” or does not exist in the database UAN showing no contribution history despite the candidate claiming years of employment Time required: Minutes using a digital verification platform. 2. Employment History Verification What to verify: Confirm previous job titles, employment dates, and the nature of the candidate’s departure from each role. How to verify: Request offer letters and relieving letters from the candidate’s last two employers Call the previous employer’s HR department directly (not the number provided by the candidate — look up the company’s official contact information independently) Verify UAN/EPF contribution records through Compose1 Verify to confirm employment timelines match provident fund deposits For senior hires, consider asking for salary slips from the last three months to verify compensation claims What to ask previous employers: “Can you confirm that [candidate name] was employed at your organization from [date] to [date]?” “What was their designation/job title?” “Is the candidate eligible for rehire?” (This question often reveals more than a direct reference) Red flags to watch for: Gaps in employment that the candidate did not disclose Job titles on the resume that differ from what the employer confirms Previous employer has no record of the candidate Candidate provides personal references instead of HR contacts at previous companies Time required: 2–5 business days per employer (manual). 24–72 hours through a BGV platform like SpringVerify. 3. Education Credential Verification What to verify: Confirm that degrees, diplomas, and certifications are genuine and were awarded by the institutions the candidate claims. How to verify: Request original degree certificates and mark sheets for physical inspection Verify directly with the university or institution — many Indian universities now offer online verification portals For professional certifications (CA, CS, engineering licenses), verify through the issuing professional body Cross-check the institution itself — is it a recognized university? The UGC’s list of recognized institutions is publicly available Red flags to watch for: Degree from an institution not recognized by UGC or AICTE Year of graduation doesn’t align with the candidate’s age or employment timeline Candidate is reluctant to provide original documents University or institution cannot be reached or does not exist at the address claimed When to prioritize this check: Education verification is most critical when the role requires specific qualifications — medical, legal, engineering, or accounting positions where practicing without valid credentials is illegal. For general business roles, it is less urgent than identity and employment verification. Time required: 3–10 business days (varies by institution responsiveness). 4. Criminal Record and Court Record Check What to verify: Determine whether the candidate has any criminal history, pending cases, or civil litigation that might affect their suitability for the role. How to verify: Database search through a BGV provider (IDfy, AuthBridge, SpringVerify) for known criminal records District court record search in the candidate’s residential and hometown districts High Court and Supreme Court docket searches for serious matters Police verification request (required for certain regulated industries) Important legal considerations: You cannot reject a candidate solely based on an arrest that did not result in a conviction Certain minor offenses may not be relevant to the role — a traffic violation should not disqualify someone from an accounting position Always obtain written consent from the candidate before initiating criminal checks Be aware of state-specific regulations on what criminal history information can be used in hiring decisions When to prioritize this check: Essential for roles involving financial responsibility, access to sensitive data, work with vulnerable populations (children, elderly, patients), security positions, and senior leadership roles. For entry-level non-sensitive roles, a database search may be sufficient without full court record searches. Time required: 24–48 hours for database checks. 3–10 business days for court record searches. 5. Address Verification What to verify: Confirm that the candidate lives (or has lived) at the address they provided, and that the address is a real, verifiable location. How to verify: Digital verification through postal records or utility databases Physical field verification by a BGV provider’s agent (most reliable but slowest and most expensive) Cross-reference the address against what appears on the candidate’s Voter ID, Driving Licence, or Aadhaar (the identity verification step may already have captured this information) When to prioritize this check: Address verification is most important when the role involves handling physical assets, when the company provides address-specific benefits (housing allowance, transport), or when industry regulations require confirmed address records. Time required: 2–7 business days depending on the method. 6. Reference Checks What to verify: Gather qualitative insights about the candidate’s work ethic, skills, interpersonal behavior, and professional conduct from people who have worked with them directly. How to conduct effective reference checks: Ask the candidate for 2–3 professional references (former managers, colleagues, or clients — not friends or family) Contact at least two references independently Prepare a consistent set of questions to ask each reference Questions to ask: “How would you describe [candidate’s] work quality and reliability?” “Can you describe a challenging situation they handled well? One they struggled with?” “If you had the opportunity, would you hire [candidate] again?” “Is there anything else you think we should know before extending an offer?” Red flags to watch for: References who cannot confirm basic facts about the candidate’s role or tenure Candidate who cannot provide professional references from recent roles References who are evasive or give scripted-sounding answers Reference contact details that connect to the candidate themselves (verify independently) Time required: 1–3 business days. 7. Digital Footprint and Social Media Review What to check: Review the candidate’s public digital presence for anything that might indicate risk, while respecting privacy boundaries. What to look for: LinkedIn profile consistency — does their LinkedIn match their resume in terms of roles, dates, and education? Public posts or behavior that might indicate risks for the role (hate speech, illegal activity, confidentiality violations) Professional reputation and contributions (GitHub, industry publications, speaking engagements) What NOT to do: Do not access private social media profiles or ask candidates for passwords Do not discriminate based on personal beliefs, political views, religion, or protected characteristics Do not use social media findings as the sole basis for rejection — always corroborate concerns through other verification steps Document your social media review criteria to ensure consistency across candidates Time required: 30 minutes per candidate. Verification Priority Matrix for Indian Startups Not every hire needs every check. Use this matrix to decide which verifications to run based on role sensitivity: Check Type Entry-Level Roles Mid-Level Roles Senior / Sensitive Roles Identity (PAN, Voter ID, DL, UAN) Required Required Required Employment History Recommended Required Required Education Credentials Optional (unless role-specific) Recommended Required Criminal Records Optional Recommended Required Address Verification Optional Optional Recommended Reference Checks Optional Recommended Required Digital Footprint Optional Optional Recommended Minimum viable verification for every hire: Run identity document verification through a platform like Compose1 Verify (PAN + Voter ID + DL + UAN). This takes minutes, costs a fraction of a full BGV, and catches the most impactful hiring risks — identity fraud, document forgery, and misrepresented work history (through UAN/EPF records). Compliance Requirements for Indian Employers Consent and Data Protection The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA) requires employers to obtain clear, informed consent from candidates before collecting, processing, or storing personal data for verification purposes. In practice, this means: Include a background verification consent clause in your offer letter or application form Clearly state which checks will be performed and how the data will be used Provide candidates with a mechanism to access, correct, or delete their data Store verification data securely with access restricted to authorized personnel Industry-Specific Requirements BFSI (Banking, Financial Services, Insurance): RBI guidelines effectively mandate background verification for all employees handling financial transactions IT/ITES: NASSCOM guidelines recommend comprehensive BGV for all employees, particularly those with access to client data Healthcare: Medical Council of India requires credential verification for medical professionals Government Contracts: Most government-facing projects require police verification and extensive background checks Record Retention Maintain verification records for the duration of employment plus 3–5 years after separation (or as required by your specific industry regulations). Store records securely and ensure they are accessible for audit purposes. Building Your BGV Process: Step-by-Step Step 1: Define your verification tiers. Create two or three verification levels based on role sensitivity (see the priority matrix above). Document these tiers so the process is consistent across all hiring decisions. Step 2: Draft your consent forms. Prepare a standard background check consent form that covers all the checks in your highest verification tier. Candidates sign this form before any verification begins. Step 3: Choose your tools. For identity verification, set up an account with Compose1 Verify — it requires no integration or sales call. For comprehensive BGV needs, evaluate providers like SpringVerify (startup-friendly), AuthBridge (enterprise-grade), or IDfy (API-first). Step 4: Integrate verification into your hiring timeline. The best time to initiate verification is after the final interview but before extending a formal offer letter. This minimizes wasted verification spend on candidates who drop out earlier in the process. Step 5: Create a standard operating procedure. Document who initiates verification requests, who reviews results, how discrepancies are handled, and how records are stored. Even if your “HR team” is one person, this documentation matters for consistency and compliance. Step 6: Train hiring managers. Ensure that everyone involved in hiring understands which checks are required for which roles, how to interpret verification reports, and what constitutes a legitimate red flag versus a minor discrepancy. Frequently Asked Questions What is the minimum background verification a startup should do? At minimum, verify every candidate’s identity documents (PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, UAN) using a platform like Compose1 Verify. This catches identity fraud, forged documents, and misrepresented employment history at a fraction of the cost of comprehensive BGV. Add employment and education checks for mid-level and senior roles. How long does a full background verification take in India? A complete background verification — covering identity, employment, education, criminal records, and address — typically takes 5–10 business days. Identity checks alone can be completed in minutes using digital platforms. The longest component is usually court record searches, which require 5–10 days. Can a startup do background verification without a BGV vendor? You can handle reference calls and document review internally, but identity verification against government databases requires access to verification APIs or platforms. Self-service tools like Compose1 Verify provide this access without requiring a vendor contract, making them ideal for startups that want to stay independent. Is background verification required by law in India? There is no single central law mandating background verification for all private employers. However, industry-specific regulations (RBI for banking, SEBI for securities, NASSCOM guidelines for IT/ITES) effectively make it a compliance requirement in many sectors. Beyond legal requirements, verification is simply sound business practice that protects against negligent hiring liability. What should I do if a verification reveals a discrepancy? Contact the candidate before making any decision. Many discrepancies — name transliteration differences, outdated addresses, minor date variations — have innocent explanations. Give the candidate an opportunity to provide updated documentation or clarification. Document the discrepancy, the candidate’s explanation, and your decision for your records. Material misrepresentation (fake degrees, fabricated employment) is legitimate grounds for withdrawing an offer. Related Shashank Yadav Leave a Reply Cancel reply

title: Qnity Powers the Industry’s Shift to Shrink and Stack at SEMICON Taiwan 2026

body_text: Qnity Powers the Industry’s Shift to Shrink and Stack at SEMICON Taiwan 2026 August 19, 2026 6:00am EDT Download as PDF Jon Kemp to deliver CEO Summit keynote as Qnity showcases the end-to-end materials platform making tomorrow's technologies possible TAIPEI, Aug. 19, 2026 — Qnity Electronics, Inc. (“Qnity”) (NYSE: Q), a premier technology solutions provider across the semiconductor value chain, will showcase its portfolio at SEMICON Taiwan, Sept. 2–4, 2026, at the Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center. Making its debut as an exhibitor at SEMICON Taiwan, Qnity will demonstrate how its materials innovation and integration expertise span the full stack, from the wafer and device level to system-level integration in advanced packages. Qnity will welcome customers, partners, industry leaders, and media at booth S7930 in the Materials Pavilion at TaiNEX 2. “The future of semiconductor innovation depends on progress in both device scaling and advanced packaging,” said Kate Dei Cas, President of Semiconductor Technologies at Qnity. “Meeting the demands of the next generation of semiconductor technologies will require new levels of innovation and collaboration across the ecosystem. At SEMICON Taiwan, we'll engage with customers, partners and industry leaders on the opportunities and challenges ahead.” Through technical presentations and product displays, Qnity will feature technologies that enable next-generation semiconductor manufacturing, supporting the growing demands of AI, high-performance computing, and advanced electronics. Highlights of Qnity's participation include: A keynote presentation by Jon Kemp , Chief Executive Officer, titled "Shrink and Stack: Redefining Semiconductor Innovation in the Angstrom Era," on Sept. 2 at 11 a.m. at the Ecosystem Executive & CEO Summit . Four technical presentations from Qnity experts spanning planarization, metallization, slurries, and advanced packaging as part of the IC Forum, Heterogeneous Integration Global Summit, Strategic Materials Conference, and TechXPOT. Attendees can learn how Qnity’s broad portfolio, deep technical expertise, and innovation leadership help customers address the challenges of AI-driven technology advancement and unlock the next generation of semiconductor performance. A technology showcase featuring solutions for advanced semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, and thermal management. Additionally, select materials innovations will be on display as part of SEMI’s Dream Fab at the entrance to TaiNEX 1. Additional opportunities to engage with Qnity include meetings with company leaders and technical experts, hospitality events, and through SEMICON Taiwan's Guided Tour Program, which brings industry associations, students, government representatives, and international business delegations to participating exhibitor booths. Building on more than 50 years of semiconductor materials innovation, Qnity partners with companies representing roughly 80% of the global semiconductor market. The company delivered 2025 net sales of approximately $4.75 billion and invests about 7% of net sales in research and development each year. In Taiwan, Qnity is continuing to strengthen its local presence and customer proximity. Announced earlier this year, the company is investing $61.5 million in a new advanced semiconductor research and manufacturing facility in Hsinchu Science Park , placing development capability even closer to the customers it serves. Customers and partners working on next-generation nodes, advanced packaging, and thermal challenges are invited to meet with the Qnity engineers and scientists who support these programs at booth S7930 in the Materials Pavilion at TaiNEX 2. To view the full agenda, learn more about Qnity’s activities at SEMICON Taiwan, and request a meeting, visitors are encouraged to explore Qnity’s virtual booth . About Qnity Qnity is a premier technology solutions provider across the semiconductor value chain, empowering AI, high performance computing, and advanced connectivity. From groundbreaking solutions for semiconductor chip manufacturing, to enabling high-speed transmission within complex electronic systems, our high-performance materials and integration expertise make tomorrow’s technologies possible. More information about the company, its businesses and solutions can be found at www.qnityelectronics.com . title: Pan American Silver Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Record quarterly shareholder returns of $300 million; Attributable silver production of 6.5 million ounces at the high end of quarterly guidance range; La Colorada Skarn project achieves an important milestone All amounts expressed in U.S. dollars unless otherwise indicated. Unaudited tabular amounts are in millions of U.S. dollars and thousands of shares, except per ounce
body_text: Record quarterly shareholder returns of $300 million; Attributable silver production of 6.5 million ounces at the high end of quarterly guidance range; La Colorada Skarn project achieves an important milestone All amounts expressed in U.S. dollars unless otherwise indicated. Unaudited tabular amounts are in millions of U.S. dollars and thousands of shares, except per ounce amounts, unless otherwise noted. VANCOUVER, British Columbia–(BUSINESS WIRE)– Pan American Silver Corp. (NYSE: PAAS) (TSX: PAAS) (“Pan American” or the “Company”) reports second quarter (“Q2 2026”) financial results. The Company will host a conference call and webcast on August 13, 2026 to discuss the results; details provided further in this news release. “Pan American delivered another quarter of strong financial results, generating $344 million in Attributable(1) free cash flow,” said Michael Steinmann, President and Chief Executive Officer. “We produced 6.5 million ounces of silver, at the upper end of our quarterly guidance, driven by continued strong performance at La Colorada and Juanicipio. Gold production was 166 thousand ounces in Q2 and we expect production to increase over the balance of the year across our operations, weighted to the fourth quarter, as we had guided last quarter.” “All-in sustaining costs in the first half of the year were below our guidance range for silver and in line for gold. In Q2, costs per ounce were primarily affected by lower gold production, higher consumables costs and increased labour-related costs and royalties, which reflect the increase in metal prices. We reiterate our 2026 Operating Outlook for production and costs, and remain focused on disciplined cost management and improving operating efficiencies.” “We returned a record $300 million to shareholders in Q2 through dividends and share repurchases. We are delivering on the enhanced shareholder return framework we announced in May, repurchasing over seven million shares to date in 2026 under our Normal Course Issuer Bid. These share repurchases increase the dividend per share, as well as increase shareholder exposure to our future free cash flow generation,” added Mr. Steinmann. “Our financial position remains robust. We ended the quarter with $1.8 billion in cash and investments, including cash attributable to our interest in Juanicipio. At the same time, we continue to invest in the safe and reliable operation of our mines and in projects that support future growth. In July, we renewed and amended our five-year senior unsecured revolving credit facility, doubling the size to $1.5 billion with an additional $750 million accordion feature, thereby increasing our total available liquidity to $3.2 billion.” “We reached an important milestone at the La Colorada Skarn project in Mexico, completing the first cut of the 588 Decline in early August 2026. This marks a significant step forward in advancing this world-class silver project,” said Mr. Steinmann. The following highlights for Q2 2026 include certain measures that are not generally accepted accounting principles (“non-GAAP”) financial measures. Please refer to the section titled “Alternative Performance (Non-GAAP) Measures” at the end of this news release for further information on these measures. Q2 2026 Results: Revenue of $1.1 billion and Attributable (1) revenue of $1.3 billion, inclusive of the Company’s 44% ownership share of revenue from Juanicipio. Net earnings of $305 million, or $0.72 basic earnings per share. A tax expense of $179 million was recorded. Adjusted earnings (2) of $308 million, or $0.73 basic adjusted earnings per share. Cash flow from operations of $320 million, net of $205 million of income taxes paid and $17 million use of cash for working capital (2). Attributable (1) cash flow from operations of $418 million, inclusive of the Company’s 44% ownership share of cash flow from Juanicipio. Due to increased profitability as a result of higher metal prices than management had assumed for the first half of the year, we are increasing the guidance range for taxes paid to $585 million to $635 million, assuming silver and gold prices of $60 per ounce and $4,000 per ounce, respectively, in the second half of 2026. Attributable(1) free cash flow(2) of $344 million, inclusive of the Company’s 44% ownership share of free cash flow from Juanicipio, and net of $205 million in taxes paid during Q2 2026, which is expected to be the highest period for taxes paid in 2026 due to the final settlement of taxes for 2025. Attributable(1) silver production of 6.47 million ounces, which was at the high end of the Company’s 2026 Quarterly Operating Outlook (3) range. Attributable(1) gold production of 165.9 thousand ounces, which was below the 2026 Quarterly Operating Outlook (3) range. Silver Segment all-in sustaining costs (“AISC”) (2)(4) of $17.80 per silver ounce were slightly above the 2026 Quarterly Operating Outlook (3) range. Gold Segment AISC (2)(5) of $1,984 per gold ounce were slightly above the 2026 Quarterly Operating Outlook (3) range. The Company reiterates its 2026 Operating Outlook (3) for silver and gold production and Silver Segment and Gold Segment AISC. Gold production is now expected to be at the low end of the annual 2026 guidance range and Gold Segment AISC is expected to be at the high end of the annual 2026 guidance range. Please refer to the “2026 Operating Outlook” section of this news release for further details. Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments of $1.8 billion as at June 30, 2026, including $97 million of cash for the Company’s 44% interest in Juanicipio. The Company’s senior unsecured revolving credit facility (the “Credit Facility”) is undrawn and Total Debt (2) of $841 million is primarily related to Senior Notes and lease obligations. Record total shareholder returns of $300 million through dividends and share repurchases. The Company repurchased for cancellation, approximately 4.4 million shares in Q2 2026 at an average price of $51.46 per share for a total consideration of approximately $224 million. Aggregate dividends paid were $76 million. As of close on August 11, 2026, the Company has repurchased a total of approximately 7.3 million shares at an average price of $49.22 per share for a total consideration of approximately $358 million. A cash dividend of $0.184 per common share , or approximately $76 million in aggregate, with respect to Q2 2026 was declared on August 12, 2026, payable on or about September 4, 2026, to holders of record of Pan American’s common shares as of the close of markets on August 24, 2026. The dividends are eligible dividends for Canadian income tax purposes. The declaration, timing, amount and payment of any future dividends remain at the discretion of the Company’s Board of Directors. (1) References to “Attributable” refer to the Company’s ownership share of results, which includes results from the operations that the Company has a 100% interest in, as well as from the operations, specifically Juanicipio and San Vicente, that the Company does not own a 100% interest in. (2) Adjusted earnings, Attributable free cash flow, AISC, working capital, total available liquidity, and Total Debt are non-GAAP measures; AISC are presented on an Attributable basis; please refer to the “Alternative Performance (Non-GAAP) Measures” section of this news release for a description of the composition and usefulness of these non-GAAP measures; please also refer to the MD&A for the period ended June 30, 2026, for a detailed reconciliation of these measures to the Q2 2026 Financial Statements. (3) The 2026 Operating Outlook and the 2026 Quarterly Operating Outlook were provided in the Company’s MD&A dated February 18, 2026. (4) Silver Segment AISC are calculated net of credits for realized revenues from all metals other than silver and are calculated per ounce of silver sold on an Attributable basis. (5) Gold Segment AISC are calculated net of credits for realized revenues from all metals other than gold and are calculated per ounce of gold sold. PROJECT UPDATES La Colorada Skarn, Mexico The Company invested $20 million of project capital on the La Colorada Skarn project during the first half of 2026 (“H1 2026”), largely for continued exploration drilling, and to advance the engineering and preliminary work for the 588 Decline Project. Development of the 588 Decline Project commenced in August 2026, and is a crucial step towards development of the La Colorada Skarn project and to advancing the expansion of the La Colorada silver mine, as described in the revised preliminary economic assessment effective March 24, 2026. The next phase of development is also advancing, with engineering for the material handling system and ventilation shafts on schedule to be presented to the Board of Directors for approval in the second half of 2026. Jacobina, Brazil The Company invested $22 million of project capital at Jacobina during H1 2026, focused on enhancing infrastructure and making certain plant improvements, while advancing studies for overall long-term operational optimizations. The key project advances during H1 2026 included: the construction of new carbon-in-pulp tanks, which are expected to be fully commissioned in August 2026; initiation of construction activities for the main substation and motor control center upgrades; and further in-fill exploration drilling directed towards expanding the mineral reserve and mineral resource base. In addition, the process plant optimization program, focused on streamlining and simplifying the process plant flow sheet, is progressing in a trade-off study through conceptual engineering. A significant evaluation of this intensive brownfield project is being undertaken to develop either an approach to upgrade the existing process plant circuitry and remove obsolete equipment in isolated stages to avoid significant disruptions to ongoing operations, or to build a new, state-of-the-art processing facility. Meanwhile, a filtration plant, filtered tailings stack, and mine paste backfill preparation plant alternatives are being evaluated independently of the process plant upgrade projects. The conceptual engineering phase of these projects is nearing completion and is expected to advance to detailed engineering over the next few months. Escobal, Guatemala The ILO 169 consultation process for Escobal continues with the Ministry of Energy and Mines (“MEM”). The Vice Minister of the Environment and other government representatives visited the Escobal mine on May 28, 2026. On June 22, 2026, the Company met with representatives from the MEM and the Vice Ministry of Sustainable Development, who reported that advisors to the Xinka have been retained for bilateral meetings between the MEM and the Xinka representatives to review consultation activities. Accordingly, a bilateral meeting was held on July 7, 2026. On July 2, 2026, the Vice Minister of the MEM was promoted to Minister. While the consultation work is continuing, there is currently no timeline for the conclusion of the Escobal ILO 169 consultation process and no date for a restart of operations at the Escobal mine. Timmins, Canada On June 1, 2026, the Company announced a conceptual plan for a phased development of new mineral resources to support potential production growth and extension of mine life at Timmins (the “Timmins Camp Project”). In May 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors approved the first phase of the project, with a total investment of $146 million to extend the shaft at the Bell Creek mine, and to construct two exploration drifts to access the Vogel and Samson deposits. The initial spending on this first phase is included in the Company’s annual 2026 project capital guidance for Timmins. Pan American plans to publish an update to the estimated mineral reserves and mineral resources for Timmins and Vogel, as of June 30, 2026, with the corporate-wide update in the third quarter of 2026. The Company also plans to release a preliminary economic assessment for the Timmins Camp Project in the first half of 2027.
